description:
FILED s473t3 (Opus triage of the 79 blessed rows whose only cause was a
`docs/sweep-bug-catalog.md` note), on main d9a2aac0.  PRE-EXISTING.
Probe: scratch/s473t3/probes/p01-sprintf-version.pl.

ROWS BEHIND IT (baselines/fail-baseline.tsv, 11 rows):
  sprintf.t 147 148 149 150 151 152 155 158 169 441 442
  (their descriptions are the `>%vd< >[version->new("1.2")]< ...` data lines)

REPRODUCER (perl 5.40.3 vs ./runpcl):
    use version;
    printf "A[%vd]\n", version->new("1.2");
    printf "B[%vd]\n", version->new("1.02");
    printf "C[%vd]\n", version::qv("1.2.3");
    printf "D[%vx]\n", version::qv("1.2.3");
    printf "E[%vd]\n", "1.22.333";        # a PLAIN string -- the control
  perl: A[1.2] B[1.2] C[1.2.3] D[1.2.3] E[49.46.50.50.46.51.51.51]
  PCL : A[49.46.50] B[49.46.48.50] then C DIES --
        "The function VERSION::PL-QV is undefined"
        (E, the plain-string control, is IDENTICAL in both -- so the `%v`
        flag itself is right; the whole divergence is the version object.)

MECHANISM: `%v` formats the ORDINAL of each character of its argument's
string form.  perl's version objects carry the original v-string, so `%vd`
reads the release components (1, 2); PCL's `lib/version.pm` shim has no such
carrier, so `%vd` reads the ordinals of the characters "1", ".", "2".  Fix
area: `sprintf-vector` in `cl/pcl-runtime.lisp` + `lib/version.pm` (the shim
must expose a v-string form, and must define `version::qv`).

CATALOG NOTE THIS REPLACES: sweep-bug-catalog.md sprintf.t, "`version->new` /
`version::qv` objects in `%vd`/`%vx` (~15t)".

FAMILY: the `lib/version.pm` shim gaps (#319 is_strict, #870 vcmp is a string
compare).  Layer: CLAUDE.md rule 9a -- the version behaviour belongs in the
SHIM, only the `%v`-reads-a-v-string mechanism belongs in the runtime.
subject: BUG (sprintf): `%vd` / `%vx` of a `version` object stringifies it character by character -- `sprintf "%vd", version->new("1.2")` is `1.2` in perl and `49.46.50` in PCL, and `version::qv` does not exist at all
